decisive_items: a 4.0 × 3.3 × 6.8 cm multiloculated, enhancing hypodense and isodense mass extending superiorly from the dome of the bladder to the posterior surface of the umbilicus
surrounding acute inflammatory stranding and minimal fluid
possible invasion into the bladder dome
response.rationale: The imaging shows a multiloculated mass from bladder dome to umbilicus with inflammation, classic for an infected urachal cyst. Urachal diverticulum (R1) is less likely as it typically communicates with bladder lumen and lacks a discrete mass. Malignancy (R6/R3) is less supported without solid enhancing nodule or calcification. UTI (R4) is contradicted by worsening despite antibiotics.

rejected.why: Urachal diverticulum usually presents as a bladder outpouching, not a multiloculated mass extending to umbilicus.
Urachal sinus typically opens at umbilicus with discharge, not a bladder-dome mass.
Adenocarcinoma would more likely show solid enhancing components or calcifications; not described.
Initial UTI diagnosis contradicted by worsening symptoms and imaging showing a mass.
Inflammatory stranding and possible invasion are nonspecific and can occur with infected cyst; no clear malignant features.
